Write a figure to an HTML file

Source: R/write_html.R
write_html.Rd

Saves a figure as a standalone web page, like htmlwidgets::saveWidget() (and plotly.py's fig.write_html()), but faster for figures with a lot of data: the page is laid out by htmlwidgets as usual, while the figure's data is written to the file directly, rather than passed through htmltools as one long string, which is scanned and copied several times. For a heatmap of 4 million values this takes a fraction of the time saveWidget() does.

Usage

write_html(
  fig,
  file,
  selfcontained = TRUE,
  libdir = NULL,
  background = "white",
  title = NULL
)

Arguments

fig

A figure (e.g. from go_figure()) or a plotly.core widget (e.g. from plotly_widget(), or a figure from plotly's plot_ly()).

file

Path of the HTML file to write.

selfcontained

Whether to embed the files the page needs in it, so that the file works on its own. Otherwise they are written to libdir.

libdir

Directory for those files when selfcontained = FALSE, relative to the directory of file (default: <name of file>_files).

background

Background color of the page.

title

Title of the page (default: the widget's name).

Value

file, invisibly.

Details

The page is the same as saveWidget() writes, except that with selfcontained = TRUE the files the page needs (plotly.js, htmlwidgets and so on) are embedded as base64 data URIs by write_html() itself, without needing pandoc.

See also

htmlwidgets::saveWidget(), save_image() for static images.

Examples

fig <- go_figure() |> add_heatmap(z = as_float32(volcano))
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".html")
write_html(fig, f)
